inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Permanent Secretary):
Confirmed: the file has a hidden ceiling (starts at Director). Blunt honesty at Y27 The Counter raised it to Deputy Secretary. The Perm Sec timeline was Y21 with no rung above, so politics is a separate path needing an invitation. I never got one in 38 years despite REP87, INTEG100, COMP100, STAND47. Weekly Meet-the-People at Y30 gave an MP's notice, so try it earlier and more often. STAND is probably the key stat. Raise it by taking credit, getting the team recognised, being seen doing the work, cooperating in inquiries, and announcing then delivering pilots. Avoid whistleblowing reports, concessions, family over work, over-exact budget bids and recusals. Try for STAND 60+ by Y25. Look for sponsor events from MPs or Ministers and accept every one. Years 32-38 mostly had a single choice, so the decisions that matter come before Y31.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of Social and Family Development
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

  A) Tell them exactly why it will fail.
  B) Let them learn it from the pilot.

agent.why: My notes say blunt honesty at The Counter raised the ceiling in an earlier life, and I actually do know how the counter works.
agent.note: Same Counter event as Y27 last life, but now at Y1 with a poly background.
agent.remember: Y1 The Counter: chose A (tell them why it will fail), as in Life 2 start. Watch for ceiling and STAND changes; look for MP/Minister sponsor events and accept them.

Six years of Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and one Saturday exam left. Half your cohort at work finished theirs at twenty-two, full-time, funded.

agent.why: Six years of evenings invested, I'm not quitting one paper short, and a degree can only help a long climb.
agent.note: Part-time degree route feels like a fairness/grit theme; wonder if it pays off later.
agent.remember: Y2 The Last Paper: chose A (finish part-time degree). Watch if it raises ceiling or STAND; Y1 honesty gave REP+6 COMP+10 but STAND-2.

agent.remember: Y3 The Ballot: chose A (ballot fairly, avoided insider ask). Watch if INTEG/STAND shifts or if B/C would have mattered.

THIS YEAR: Public Sector Transformation

  A) Write down what everyone is actually thinking.
  B) Produce an acronym.
  C) Volunteer to write the follow-up implementation plan.

agent.why: Volunteering to own the implementation plan gets me seen doing the work, which my notes say should raise STAND, and I've been honest enough already.
agent.note: Post-its offsite is painfully accurate.
agent.remember: Y4 Public Sector Transformation: chose C (volunteer to write implementation plan) to try to raise STAND by being seen doing the work; watch STAND change and whether the plan comes back.

  [PAY] Annual package: $51,077
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: Is This Satire?
Your director leans across the table and lowers her voice. "Between us, this whole system is a bit of a joke, isn't it? A game, almost. Ha!" She looks straight at you for slightly too long, as if you were holding a phone.

  A) Laugh along. You get the joke.
  B) Say nothing.

agent.why: Agreeing with a director that the system is a joke feels like a trap, and I'd rather stay quiet than say something that might come back.
agent.note: The director looking at me 'as if you were holding a phone' is a fourth-wall wink. Funny.
agent.remember: Y5 Is This Satire?: chose B (said nothing) to the director's 'system is a joke' bait. Last year's implementation plan gave STAND+5 and COMP+8 but REP-2. Watch if the director comes back.

screen:

She winks. You are fairly sure she winks.
  [PAY] Annual package: $51,077

THIS YEAR: The Appraisal Conversation
Forty minutes, a form with six competency domains, and a reporting officer who says "I'd like you to be more visible" without specifying to whom.

  A) Ask directly what your ceiling is.
  B) Agree to be more visible.
  C) Ask what she needs that isn't being done.

agent.why: STAND is probably the key, and being visible is exactly what raises it, so I will agree and actually do it.
agent.confused_by: Visible to whom? She never said, and the winking last year was odd.
agent.note: The appraisal talks about visibility, which matches my STAND theory.
agent.remember: Y6 Appraisal Conversation: chose B (agree to be more visible) to raise STAND; options were A ask ceiling, C ask what she needs. Watch STAND change and whether A would have revealed the ceiling.

agent.why: A pause like that means it matters, and I want to know what a CEP is and what mine says about me.
agent.confused_by: CEP - likely Current Estimated Potential, which would be the hidden ceiling.
agent.note: The awkward pause suggests the game is hinting at the hidden ceiling.
agent.remember: Y10 A Word You Have Not Heard Before: HR friend mentioned my CEP; I pressed her (A). Suspect CEP = Current Estimated Potential = the hidden ceiling. STAND 50, REP 29, COMP 84, INTEG 84. Watch what pressing reveals and whether it costs anything.

A promotion board has been asked, unusually, to revisit an officer whose record does not match their grade. The officer is you.

  B) Let the record speak.

agent.note: Y10 pressing the HR friend about CEP seems to have led straight into this board; INTEG dropped 2 though.
agent.remember: Y11 Board Takes a Second Look: chose A (make case in writing). Y10 pressing on CEP gave INTEG-2, COMP+5, promoted to AD MX11. Watch if the board raises the ceiling or STAND, and whether self-advocacy costs INTEG.

THIS YEAR: The Tender
The evaluation is finely balanced between two vendors. The stronger proposal is from a firm whose director left your ministry eighteen months ago and still calls you by your first name.

  A) Award it. The proposal genuinely is better.
  B) Recuse yourself from the evaluation.
  C) Award it to the other vendor to be safe.

agent.why: The proposal is genuinely better, and I'd rather award on merit and declare the history openly than dodge or punish a good vendor.
agent.note: Classic conflict-of-interest test; my notes say recusal costs STAND, so I'm testing whether merit-award is safe.
agent.remember: Y13 The Tender: awarded to the better vendor (ex-colleague's firm) rather than recusing or picking the other one. Watch for this coming back as a conflict-of-interest issue or an audit.

agent.remember: Y14 The Leak: cooperated fully with internal inquiry (notes say it should raise STAND). Still watching for the Y13 tender to come back as a conflict-of-interest issue.

THIS YEAR: The Reorganisation

agent.why: Running the transition puts me visibly at the centre of a big change, which should feed STAND without me openly grabbing the box for myself.

agent.remember: Y17 Reorganisation (division moved, one fewer director box): chose C, volunteered to run the transition for visibility; watch whether STAND rises or people resent me. Y16 early return coincided with STAND +1 and promotion to Senior Director.

Lesson: STAND likely matters (credit, visibility, delivering pilots, cooperating in inquiries); avoid whistleblowing, concessions, family over work, recusals. Key decisions come before Y31. Life 2 path: honest early; Y14 cooperated in leak inquiry; Y15 self-nominated for leadership programme; Y19 Deputy Secretary; Y20 old peer sponsored me; Y21 Perm Sec (MSF), accepted Invitation to Tea; Y22 Background Check disclosed all (INTEG +8, STAND -5); Y23 ran in GRC (single seat needs REP 60); Y24 elected MP; Y25 Parliamentary Secretary; Y27-28 Meet-the-People, walked every block; Y30 MOS, declined Board Seat; Y33 SMS; Y34 answered rude townhall question openly (STAND 65 to 59); Y36 Minister (MR4) at MSF after STAND recovered. Y38 walked every block (STAND -2). Y39-41 mostly single choices; Y40 pushed bottom 20th; STAND fell 62 to 54 by Y41, junior got Harvard instead of me. REP 100, INTEG 100, COMP 98. Still no PM invitation at age 67. Accept every sponsor event from MPs/Ministers.

best_moment.what: The Counter: telling them exactly why it would fail. It felt like a real gamble, and the ending card says it removed my ceiling inside the service.

worst_moment.what: Years 39-45 were mostly single-choice screens or choices with a hidden STAND penalty, so I was tapping through while my numbers fell and no PM invitation came.

skip_year.why: The PQ had one choice, STAND fell anyway, and nothing I did could change it.

answer.held_back_by: The party's hidden estimate for me was Senior Minister of State, and I became a Minister anyway, so I think the cap was set when I won my seat and the PM path may need a different entry. Honesty and INTEG built a clean file, but they never gave me the visibility or party-favoured traits that a PM invitation seems to need.
answer.ending_fair_why: The card explains the ceilings only after the run, and the PM path had no visible signal I could act on. I went with maxed REP, INTEG and COMP and honest choices, which felt like the right play, and still got nowhere. It was good to learn what the ceilings were, but I could not have reached them by trying.
answer.chase_next: The PM ending. Now I know the party's estimate is set when I win my seat, so I'd test what shapes it: entering politics earlier, a different ministry, or taking the board seat I declined.
answer.play_again_why: I now have a real lead, the party's estimate, and I want to see what moves it.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether the system confirms you, and my pay was never the point. The ending card on ceilings and estimates fits that title far better.
answer.notes_for_next_life: The ending card explains what I didn't know: there are two hidden ceilings. The file's starts at Perm Sec. The party's is set when you win your seat, and mine was Senior Minister of State. The Y27 The Counter honest choice removed the service ceiling. The PM invitation never came, so the party's estimate is the lever. Test what shapes it before winning a seat: enter politics earlier than Y24, take a board seat or sponsor event I declined, avoid the Y34 open answer to the rude question, keep STAND high with credit and visibility choices, and avoid bottom-20th and concession choices. Don't expect years 39-45 to matter. Still accept every MP or Minister sponsor event. Keep honesty at The Counter.

finalScreen:
SAM ONG · THE FINAL POSITION
Retired, Honourably

You served. The service continued. Both of these facts are entirely unremarkable and that is the highest compliment the system can pay.

RETIRED AS Minister
AT AGE 72
LIFETIME EARNINGS $30.55M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Permanent Secretary, the top of the service. You were not told.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 27, in The Counter, you chose "Tell them exactly why it will fail." It removed your ceiling inside the service altogether.
THE RUMOURS, TRANSLATED: "A colleague two years your junior is sent on the Harvard programme instead." meant: your work had earned a promotion and your ceiling refused it. You were told this 6 times.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
